'''Francis Patrick Crotty''' (11 April 1938 – 18 December 2016) was a New Zealand [[Rowing (sport)|rower]] and industrial chemist.

== Early life ==
Born in [[Foxton, New Zealand|Foxton]] on 11 April 1938, Crotty was the son of Thomas Vincent Crotty and Lucy Pearl Crotty (née Thompson).<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.genealogy.com/ftm/g/a/u/Raymond-Gaudening/WEBSITE-0001/UHP-0033.html | title=Information about Francis Patrick (Frank) Crotty | publisher=Genealogy.com | first=Raymond | last=Gauden-Ing | accessdate=13 January 2017}}</ref> In 1956, he began studying at [[Victoria University of Wellington|Victoria University College]],<ref>{{cite news | url=http://nzetc.victoria.ac.nz/tm/scholarly/tei-Salient20021956-t1-body-d22.html | title=Tournament invasion | work=Salient | date=29 March 1956 | volume=20 | number=2 | accessdate=13 January 2017 | page=5}}</ref> graduating with a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1961.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university6.html | title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: Co–Cu | accessdate=13 January 2017}}</ref>

== Rowing ==
A member of the Union Boat Club in [[Whanganui]], Crotty was in the winning Union four with [[Donald Gemmell]], Dave Martin and [[Allan Tong]] at the New Zealand championships in 1957.<ref name="UBC obituary">{{cite web | url=http://unionboatclub.co.nz/2017/01/08/passing-of-frank-crotty/ | title=Passing of Frank Crotty | date=8 January 2017 | publisher=Union Boat Club Whanganui | accessdate=13 January 2017}}</ref> The following year he again won the national fours title, this time with Gemmell, [[Peter Aitchison (rower)|Peter Aitchison]], [[Graeme Moran]] and [[Richard Tuffin]] ([[Coxswain (rowing)|coxswain]]), and the same crew went on to represent New Zealand at the [[New Zealand at the 1958 British Empire and Commonwealth Games|1958 British Empire and Commonwealth Games]] in Cardiff, finishing fourth.<ref name="UBC obituary"/><ref name="Rotary bio">{{cite web | url=http://www.taradalerotary.co.nz/paul_harris_rotary_awards.htm | title=Paul Harris Fellows | publisher=Rotary Club of Taradale | accessdate=13 January 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170406061006/http://taradalerotary.co.nz/paul_harris_rotary_awards.htm | archive-date=6 April 2017 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Career ==
Crotty worked for the Southland Frozen Meat Company in [[Invercargill]] and completed a [[Master of Science]] degree studying extramurally. In the late 1960s, Crotty and his family moved to [[Hawke's Bay Region|Hawke's Bay]] where he was employed at the East Coast Fertiliser Works as production supervisor and chief chemist. In 1977, he took up the position of works manager at the New Zealand Farmers’ Fertiliser Company in [[New Plymouth]], and in 1984 he was appointed general manager of Moa-Nui Cooperative Dairies in [[Inglewood, New Zealand|Inglewood]].<ref name="Rotary bio" />

Crotty joined [[Rotary International|Rotary]] in New Plymouth, serving as president of the New Plymouth North Rotary Club and district governor's representative in 1981–82. He continued his involvement with Rotary after moving to Hawke's Bay in 1992 as a member of the [[Taradale, New Zealand|Taradale]] club. In 2010, Crotty was awarded the [[Paul Harris Fellow]]ship.<ref name="Rotary bio" />

== Family life ==
In 1963, Crotty married Julia Monro,<ref name="Rotary bio" /> and the couple went on to have five children.<ref name="Death notice" /> Crotty and his wife returned to Hawke's Bay in 1992, where they bought and ran a vineyard that they ran until retiring in 1999.

== Death ==
Crotty died at his home in Taradale on 18 December 2016.<ref name="Death notice">{{cite news | url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/hawkesbaytoday-nz/obituary.aspx?n=francis-patrick-crotty-frank&pid=183193659 | title=Francis Crotty death notice | date=24 December 2016 | work=Hawkes Bay Today | accessdate=13 January 2017}}</ref>
